page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. This x86_64 architecture server features 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core. It is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include bundled local storage or GPU hardware, and it offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The instance demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25%, and average single-core performance in Geekbench and text processing. However, multi-core performance is weak, falling into the bottom 25% for stress-ng and the bottom 10% for Geekbench multi-core, software compilation, and ray tracing. Memory performance is also constrained, with read-only small block memory bandwidth and PassMark memory scores ranking in the bottom 10%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n2d-standard-2 offers a dedicated CPU allocation at a low entry point, making it suitable for lightweight workloads that require consistent CPU access without the unpredictability of burstable instances. However, the low memory bandwidth and poor multi-core scaling present clear tradeoffs. It is best suited for basic web serving, lightweight single-threaded applications, text processing, and development or testing environments that do not demand high parallel processing power or intensive database operations.
